key_insight: Calcium channel blockers reduce arterial media stress but can shift load to the fibrous cap, potentially increasing plaque rupture risk if blood pressure is insufficiently reduced.
engineering_relevance: Coupled drug-transport and arterial-mechanics simulations can reveal local stress changes that may be missed when assessing treatment through blood pressure alone.
method: Couple 3D reaction–diffusion drug transport with finite element arterial mechanics.
Model calcium-dependent smooth muscle contraction, nonlinear anisotropic tissue behavior, and residual stresses.
Fit material parameters to published experiments and simulate five histology-derived atherosclerotic geometries.
evidence_signal: Fibrous-cap stress increased in all five geometries, with median increases up to 28.9 kPa; a 10 mmHg blood pressure reduction limited median increases to at most 3.8 kPa in four geometries.
watch_item: Predicted rupture-risk implications require experimental and clinical confirmation; the study evaluates only five exemplary geometries.
paper_title: Pharmaco-mechanical computational simulation of atherosclerotic arteries: effects of calcium channel blockers on local stress distributions
